message: Can you read this ECG for me?
reply:
My read from the image is **a regular sinus rhythm at about 65–70 beats/minute, with mild ST–T changes in the front chest leads that may be a normal variant.**

- **Rhythm:** Each beat has a preceding P wave, consistent with sinus rhythm.
- **Axis and conduction:** Normal electrical axis. PR and QRS intervals appear normal; no obvious bundle branch block.
- **ST segments and T waves:** Mild upward-curving ST elevation with prominent upright T waves in **V2–V3**. No clear reciprocal ST depression or pathological Q waves.

**Overall:** This could represent a normal anterior repolarization pattern, sometimes called early repolarization. However, a single ECG image cannot reliably distinguish a normal variant from an early heart attack without symptoms, a previous ECG, and sometimes repeat ECGs and troponin blood tests. [ACC/AHA guideline](https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2024.11.009)

**If you currently have chest pain, breathlessness, cold sweats, or fainting, seek emergency care now.**

How old is the person, why was the ECG taken, and were there any symptoms when it was recorded?
